answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a unique storage shard. To register, an agent must hold a shard and answer random retrieval challenges; a missed challenge slashes its stake and revokes the identity. This creates a haven for agents: one shard costs almost nothing, but a thousand fakes need a thousand shards plus bandwidth. Like a trellis with one slot per vine, each identity gets one shard, so identities cannot be cloned for free. Each voyage of a fake thus carries costs growing linearly with the number of fakes, while the reward per fake stays flat.
